      "text": "Here are the digitized, structured, and analyzed notes based on the provided lecture material. The notes cover **Rotational Dynamics**, **Circular Motion**, and **System Dynamics with Moments of Inertia**.\n\nThe source material is in Slovenian; I have retained the original variable notation (e.g., $F_v$ for rope force/tension, $F_{tr}$ for friction) but provided English explanations and derivations.\n\n***\n\n# [[Rotational Dynamics]] \u0026 Systems of Particles\n\n**Date:** 2025-11-20\n**Tags:** #physics #mechanics #rotation #newtons-laws #derivations\n**Source Material:** Lecture Notes (Images 1-8)\n\n---\n\n## 1. Vertical Circular Motion (The Loop)\n\nThe lecture begins with an object moving in a vertical circle (e.g., a roller coaster loop or a stone on a string).\n\n### **Physical Model**\n*   **Top of the loop:** Gravity ($F_g$) and Normal Force ($F_N$) both point downward (towards the center).\n*   **Bottom of the loop:** Gravity points down (outward), Normal Force points up (inward).\n\n### **Key Equations**\nFrom [[Newton\u0027s Second Law]] ($\\sum \\vec{F} \u003d m\\vec{a}$):\n\n1.  **Centripetal Acceleration:**\n    $$ a_{cp} \u003d \\omega^2 r \u003d \\frac{v^2}{r} $$\n    Where:\n    *   $\\omega$ \u003d angular velocity\n    *   $v$ \u003d tangential velocity\n    *   $r$ \u003d radius\n\n2.  **Force Balance at the Top (Critical Point):**\n    $$ F_N + F_g \u003d m a_{cp} \u003d m \\omega^2 r $$\n    *Condition for weightlessness (losing contact):* $F_N \u003d 0$.\n    $$ F_g \u003d m \\omega^2 r \\implies mg \u003d m \\omega^2 r \\implies g \u003d \\omega^2 r $$\n\n### **Derivation of Coefficient $k_l$**\nThe notes calculate a coefficient $k_l$, likely relating the centripetal force to the gravitational force (a \"g-force\" factor).\n\n$$ k_l \u003d \\frac{\\omega^2 r_{max}}{g} $$\n\n**From the notes:**\nGiven: $t_0 \u003d 3.14 s$ (Period $T$), $r \u003d 0.1m$? (The handwriting implies $r\u003d10cm\u003d0.1m$).\n$$ \\omega \u003d \\frac{2\\pi}{T} \\approx 2 \\, \\text{rad/s} $$\n$$ k_l \u003d \\frac{(2\\,s^{-1})^2 \\cdot 0.1\\,m}{9.81\\,m/s^2} \\approx 0.0408 $$\n\n\u003e [!NOTE] **Tutor\u0027s Insight:**\n\u003e The value $k_l \\approx 0.04$ is very small. This implies the rotation is quite slow for the given radius, or the radius is small. If this were a roller coaster, the passengers would fall out at the top because $a_{cp} \u003c g$. For the passengers to stay in, we need $a_{cp} \\geq g$, or $k_l \\geq 1$.\n\n---\n\n## 2. [[Earth\u0027s Rotation]] and Effective Gravity\n\nThe lecture moves to the effect of Earth\u0027s rotation on the perceived acceleration due to gravity ($g$).\n\n### **Setup**\n*   **Radius of Earth ($R_z$):** $6400 \\, \\text{km} \u003d 6.4 \\times 10^6 \\, \\text{m}$\n*   **Standard Gravity ($g_0$):** $9.83 \\, \\text{m/s}^2$ (at poles)\n*   **Period ($t_0$):** 1 day ($86400 \\, \\text{s}$)\n\n### **Analysis**\nAt the equator, the Earth spins, creating a \"centrifugal\" effect that counters gravity. The measured weight is the Normal force ($F_N$).\n\n$$ \\sum F \u003d m a_{cp} $$\n$$ F_g - F_N \u003d m a_{cp} $$\n$$ F_N \u003d F_g - m a_{cp} $$\n\nThe **Effective Gravity** ($g\u0027$) is defined by $F_N \u003d m g\u0027$:\n$$ m g\u0027 \u003d m g_0 - m \\omega_z^2 R_z $$\n$$ g\u0027 \u003d g_0 - \\omega_z^2 R_z $$\n\n### **Calculation of Relative Change ($\\frac{\\Delta g}{g_0}$)**\nAngular velocity of Earth:\n$$ \\omega_z \u003d \\frac{2\\pi}{86400\\,s} \\approx 7.27 \\times 10^{-5} \\, \\text{s}^{-1} $$\n\nCentripetal acceleration at equator:\n$$ a_{cp} \u003d \\omega_z^2 R_z \\approx (7.27 \\times 10^{-5})^2 \\cdot (6.4 \\times 10^6) \\approx 0.034 \\, \\text{m/s}^2 $$\n\nRelative change:\n$$ \\frac{\\Delta g}{g_0} \u003d \\frac{g_{eff} - g_0}{g_0} \u003d -\\frac{\\omega_z^2 R_z}{g_0} $$\n$$ \\frac{\\Delta g}{g_0} \\approx -\\frac{0.034}{9.83} \\approx -0.0034 \u003d -0.34\\% $$\n\n\u003e [!success] **Conclusion**\n\u003e Objects weigh approximately **0.34% less** at the equator than at the poles due to Earth\u0027s rotation.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Dynamics of Machinery (The Heavy [[Pulley System]])\n\nThis section solves a coupled system involving translation and rotation.\n\n### **System Diagram**\n*   **Body 1 ($m$):** Hanging mass ($1 \\, \\text{kg}$).\n*   **Body 2 ($M$):** Mass on horizontal surface ($3 \\, \\text{kg}$).\n*   **Pulley (Škripec):** Has mass and [[Moment of Inertia]] ($J^* \u003d 10^{-2} \\, \\text{kg m}^2$). Radius $R \u003d 10 \\, \\text{cm} \u003d 0.1 \\, \\text{m}$.\n*   **Friction:** Coefficient $k_t \u003d 0.1$.\n\n### **Equations of Motion**\nWe apply Newton\u0027s 2nd Law for translation and rotation. We must treat the tension in the rope as **different** on either side of the massive pulley ($F_{v1} \\neq F_{v2}$).\n\n1.  **Body 2 (Horizontal Motion):**\n    $$ F_{v1} - F_{tr} \u003d M \\cdot a $$\n    Where friction $F_{tr} \u003d k_t \\cdot M \\cdot g$.\n    $$ \\Rightarrow F_{v1} - k_t Mg \u003d Ma $$\n\n2.  **Pulley (Rotational Motion):**\n    $$ \\sum M \u003d J^* \\cdot \\alpha $$\n    The torque is caused by the difference in tensions.\n    $$ (F_{v2} - F_{v1}) \\cdot R \u003d J^* \\cdot \\alpha $$\n    *Constraint:* Linear acceleration $a \u003d R \\cdot \\alpha \\implies \\alpha \u003d \\frac{a}{R}$.\n    $$ F_{v2} - F_{v1} \u003d \\frac{J^* a}{R^2} $$\n\n3.  **Body 1 (Vertical Motion):**\n    $$ F_g - F_{v2} \u003d m \\cdot a $$\n    $$ m \\cdot g - F_{v2} \u003d m \\cdot a $$\n\n### **Solving the System**\nTo find acceleration $a$, we sum the equations effectively to eliminate internal tensions ($F_{v1}, F_{v2}$).\n\n**Step 1: Isolate Tensions**\n*   From (1): $F_{v1} \u003d Ma + k_t Mg$\n*   From (3): $F_{v2} \u003d mg - ma$\n\n**Step 2: Substitute into Torque Equation (2)**\n$$ (mg - ma) - (Ma + k_t Mg) \u003d \\frac{J^* a}{R^2} $$\n\n**Step 3: Group terms with $a$**\n$$ mg - k_t Mg \u003d ma + Ma + \\frac{J^*}{R^2} a $$\n$$ g(m - k_t M) \u003d a \\left( m + M + \\frac{J^*}{R^2} \\right) $$\n\n**Step 4: Final Formula for Acceleration**\n$$ a \u003d g \\cdot \\frac{m - k_t M}{m + M + \\frac{J^*}{R^2}} $$\n\n\u003e [!tldr] **Interpretation of the Result**\n\u003e The numerator represents the **net driving force** (Gravity on hanging mass minus Friction on sliding mass).\n\u003e The denominator represents the **total inertia** of the system (Mass 1 + Mass 2 + Effective mass of the pulley $\\frac{J^*}{R^2}$).\n\n**Calculation (from notes):**\n$$ a \u003d 9.81 \\cdot \\frac{1 - 0.1(3)}{1 + 3 + \\frac{0.01}{0.1^2}} \u003d 9.81 \\cdot \\frac{0.7}{4 + 1} \u003d 9.81 \\cdot \\frac{0.7}{5} \\approx 1.37 \\, \\text{m/s}^2 $$\n*(Note: The student\u0027s note calculation resulted in 5.8. Let\u0027s check the student\u0027s specific values. In the image, the result is $a\u003d5.8$, but checking the math: $\\frac{J^*}{R^2} \u003d \\frac{10^{-2}}{10^{-2}} \u003d 1$. Denom is $1+3+1 \u003d 5$. Numerator $1 - 0.3 \u003d 0.7$. $0.7/5 \\cdot 10 \u003d 1.4$. The student likely used different mass values later or made a calculation error. **Warning: Check inputs.**)*\n\n---\n\n## 4. Rolling Motion and Moment of Inertia\n\nCalculation of Moment of Inertia for a specific cylinder/wheel setup.\n\n*   **Given:** $a_t \u003d 0.16 \\, \\text{m/s}^2$ (Tangential acceleration?), Force $F\u003d10N$, $m\u003d10kg$, $R\u003d0.3m$.\n*   **Equation:** $F_t \\cdot R \u003d J^* \\cdot \\alpha \u003d J^* \\frac{a_t}{R}$\n*   **Result:** $J^* \u003d \\frac{F_t R^2}{a_t}$\n*   **Calculation in notes:**\n    $$ J^* \u003d \\frac{4N \\cdot 0.09m^2}{0.6} \u003d 0.6 \\, \\text{kg m}^2 $$\n    *(Note: Here $F_t$ is derived as $F - ma$, likely the net force causing torque).*\n\n---\n\n## 5. Comprehensive System Solution (Summary Strategy)\n\nThe final part of the notes (Images 7 \u0026 8) formalizes the \"System of Equations\" approach. Instead of substitution, you can write the equations vertically and sum them.\n\n$$\n\\begin{align}\n\\text{Eq 1 (Sliding):} \u0026 \\quad F_{v1} - F_{tr} \u003d M a \\\\\n\\text{Eq 2 (Pulley):} \u0026 \\quad F_{v2} - F_{v1} \u003d \\frac{J^*}{R^2} a \\\\\n\\text{Eq 3 (Hanging):} \u0026 \\quad m g - F_{v2} \u003d m a\n\\end{align}\n$$\n\n**Summing Left and Right sides:**\nThe internal tensions $+F_{v1}, -F_{v1}$ and $+F_{v2}, -F_{v2}$ cancel out perfectly.\n\n$$ m g - F_{tr} \u003d a \\left( M + \\frac{J^*}{R^2} + m \\right) $$\n\nThis confirms the derivation in Section 3 and is a faster method for solving these problems during exams.\n\n### **Specific Example: Cart on a Hill**\n*   **Scenario:** A cart (10kg) with force 10N acts on it.       "parts": [{
        "text": "Here are the digitized, structured, and analyzed notes based on the provided lecture material. The notes cover **Rotational Dynamics**, **"
      }, {
        "text": "Circular Motion**, and **System Dynamics with Moments of Inertia**.\n\nThe source material is in Slovenian; I have retained"
      }, {
        "text": " the original variable notation (e.g., $F_v$ for rope force/tension, $F_{tr}$"
      }, {
        "text": " for friction) but provided English explanations and derivations.\n\n***\n\n# [[Rotational Dynamics]] \u0026 Systems of Particles\n\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "Date:** 2025-11-20\n**Tags:** #physics #mechanics #rotation #new"
      }, {
        "text": "tons-laws #derivations\n**Source Material:** Lecture Notes (Images 1-8)\n\n---\n\n## 1. Vertical Circular Motion"
      }, {
        "text": " (The Loop)\n\nThe lecture begins with an object moving in a vertical circle (e.g., a roller coaster"
      }, {
        "text": " loop or a stone on a string).\n\n### **Physical Model**\n*   **Top of the loop:** Gravity"
      }, {
        "text": " ($F_g$) and Normal Force ($F_N$) both point downward (towards the center).\n*   **Bottom"
      }, {
        "text": " of the loop:** Gravity points down (outward), Normal Force points up (inward).\n\n### **Key Equations**\nFrom"
      }, {
        "text": " [[Newton\u0027s Second Law]] ($\\sum \\vec{F} \u003d m\\vec{a}$):\n\n1.  **Centrip"
      }, {
        "text": "etal Acceleration:**\n    $$ a_{cp} \u003d \\omega^2 r \u003d \\frac{v^2}{"
      }, {
        "text": "r} $$\n    Where:\n    *   $\\omega$ \u003d angular velocity\n    *   $v$ \u003d tangential"
      }, {
        "text": " velocity\n    *   $r$ \u003d radius\n\n2.  **Force Balance at the Top (Critical Point):**\n    $$"
      }, {
        "text": " F_N + F_g \u003d m a_{cp} \u003d m \\omega^2 r $$\n    *"
      }, {
        "text": "Condition for weightlessness (losing contact):* $F_N \u003d 0$.\n    $$ F_g \u003d m \\omega^2"
      }, {
        "text": " r \\implies mg \u003d m \\omega^2 r \\implies g \u003d \\omega^2 r $$\n\n### **Derivation of Coefficient"
      }, {
        "text": " $k_l$**\nThe notes calculate a coefficient $k_l$, likely relating the centripetal force to"
      }, {
        "text": " the gravitational force (a \"g-force\" factor).\n\n$$ k_l \u003d \\frac{\\omega^2 r_{max}}{g"
      }, {
        "text": "} $$\n\n**From the notes:**\nGiven: $t_0 \u003d 3.14 s$ (Period"
      }, {
        "text": " $T$), $r \u003d 0.1m$? (The handwriting implies $r\u003d10cm\u003d0.1m$).\n$$"
      }, {
        "text": " \\omega \u003d \\frac{2\\pi}{T} \\approx 2 \\, \\text{rad/s} $$"
      }, {
        "text": "\n$$ k_l \u003d \\frac{(2\\,s^{-1})^2 \\cdot 0.1\\,m}{9.81\\,m"
      }, {
        "text": "/s^2} \\approx 0.0408 $$\n\n\u003e [!NOTE] **Tutor\u0027s Insight"
      }, {
        "text": ":**\n\u003e The value $k_l \\approx 0.04$ is very small. This implies the rotation"
      }, {
        "text": " is quite slow for the given radius, or the radius is small. If this were a roller coaster, the passengers would fall out"
      }, {
        "text": " at the top because $a_{cp} \u003c g$. For the passengers to stay in, we need $a_{cp} \\geq"
      }, {
        "text": " g$, or $k_l \\geq 1$.\n\n---\n\n## 2. [[Earth\u0027s Rotation]]"
      }, {
        "text": " and Effective Gravity\n\nThe lecture moves to the effect of Earth\u0027s rotation on the perceived acceleration due to gravity ($g$).\n\n### **"
      }, {
        "text": "Setup**\n*   **Radius of Earth ($R_z$):** $6400 \\, \\text{km}"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d 6.4 \\times 10^6 \\, \\text{m}$\n*   **Standard Gravity"
      }, {
        "text": " ($g_0$):** $9.83 \\, \\text{m/s}^2$ (at"
      }, {
        "text": " poles)\n*   **Period ($t_0$):** 1 day ($86400 \\, \\text"
      }, {
        "text": "{s}$)\n\n### **Analysis**\nAt the equator, the Earth spins, creating a \"centrifugal\" effect that counters"
      }, {
        "text": " gravity. The measured weight is the Normal force ($F_N$).\n\n$$ \\sum F \u003d m a_{cp}"
      }, {
        "text": " $$\n$$ F_g - F_N \u003d m a_{cp} $$\n$$ F_N \u003d F"
      }, {
        "text": "_g - m a_{cp} $$\n\nThe **Effective Gravity** ($g\u0027$) is defined by $F_N \u003d m"
      }, {
        "text": " g\u0027$:\n$$ m g\u0027 \u003d m g_0 - m \\omega_z^2 R_z $$\n"
      }, {
        "text": "$$ g\u0027 \u003d g_0 - \\omega_z^2 R_z $$\n\n### **Calculation of Relative"
      }, {
        "text": " Change ($\\frac{\\Delta g}{g_0}$)**\nAngular velocity of Earth:\n$$ \\omega_z \u003d \\frac{2\\"
      }, {
        "text": "pi}{86400\\,s} \\approx 7.27 \\times 10^{-5"
      }, {
        "text": "} \\, \\text{s}^{-1} $$\n\nCentripetal acceleration at equator:\n$$ a_{cp} \u003d \\omega_"
      }, {
        "text": "z^2 R_z \\approx (7.27 \\times 10^{-5})^2 \\cdot (6.4 \\times "
      }, {
        "text": "10^6) \\approx 0.034 \\, \\text{m/s}^2 $$\n\n"
      }, {
        "text": "Relative change:\n$$ \\frac{\\Delta g}{g_0} \u003d \\frac{g_{eff} -"
      }, {
        "text": " g_0}{g_0} \u003d -\\frac{\\omega_z^2 R_z}{g_0"
      }, {
        "text": "} $$\n$$ \\frac{\\Delta g}{g_0} \\approx -\\frac{0.034}{9.83"
      }, {
        "text": "} \\approx -0.0034 \u003d -0.34\\% $$\n\n\u003e [!success] **Conclusion"
      }, {
        "text": "**\n\u003e Objects weigh approximately **0.34% less** at the equator than at the poles due to Earth\u0027s rotation.\n\n---\n\n"
      }, {
        "text": "## 3. Dynamics of Machinery (The Heavy [[Pulley System]])\n\nThis section solves a coupled system involving translation"
      }, {
        "text": " and rotation.\n\n### **System Diagram**\n*   **Body 1 ($m$):** Hanging mass ($"
      }, {
        "text": "1 \\, \\text{kg}$).\n*   **Body 2 ($M$):** Mass on horizontal surface ($"
      }, {
        "text": "3 \\, \\text{kg}$).\n*   **Pulley (Škripec):** Has mass and [[Moment of Inertia]]"
      }, {
        "text": " ($J^* \u003d 10^{-2} \\, \\text{kg m}^2$). Radius $R \u003d "
      }, {
        "text": "10 \\, \\text{cm} \u003d 0.1 \\, \\text{m}$.\n*   **F"
      }, {
        "text": "riction:** Coefficient $k_t \u003d 0.1$.\n\n### **Equations of Motion**\nWe apply Newton\u0027s 2nd Law for"
      }, {
        "text": " translation and rotation. We must treat the tension in the rope as **different** on either side of the massive pulley ($F_{v1}"
      }, {
        "text": " \\neq F_{v2}$).\n\n1.  **Body 2 (Horizontal Motion):**\n    $$ F_{v1} - F_{"
      }, {
        "text": "tr} \u003d M \\cdot a $$\n    Where friction $F_{tr} \u003d k_t \\cdot M"
      }, {
        "text": " \\cdot g$.\n    $$ \\Rightarrow F_{v1} - k_t Mg \u003d Ma $$\n\n2.  **Pul"
      }, {
        "text": "ley (Rotational Motion):**\n    $$ \\sum M \u003d J^* \\cdot \\alpha $$\n    The torque is"
      }, {
        "text": " caused by the difference in tensions.\n    $$ (F_{v2} - F_{v1}) \\cdot"
      }, {
        "text": " R \u003d J^* \\cdot \\alpha $$\n    *Constraint:* Linear acceleration $a \u003d R \\cdot \\alpha \\"
      }, {
        "text": "implies \\alpha \u003d \\frac{a}{R}$.\n    $$ F_{v2} - F_{v1} \u003d \\"
      }, {
        "text": "frac{J^* a}{R^2} $$\n\n3.  **Body 1 (Vertical Motion):**\n    $$"
      }, {
        "text": " F_g - F_{v2} \u003d m \\cdot a $$\n    $$ m \\cdot g - F_{v2"
      }, {
        "text": "} \u003d m \\cdot a $$\n\n### **Solving the System**\nTo find acceleration $a$, we sum the"
      }, {
        "text": " equations effectively to eliminate internal tensions ($F_{v1}, F_{v2}$).\n\n**Step 1: Is"
      }, {
        "text": "olate Tensions**\n*   From (1): $F_{v1} \u003d Ma + k_t Mg$"
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   From (3): $F_{v2} \u003d mg - ma$\n\n**Step 2:"
      }, {
        "text": " Substitute into Torque Equation (2)**\n$$ (mg - ma) - (Ma + k_t Mg) \u003d \\frac{"
      }, {
        "text": "J^* a}{R^2} $$\n\n**Step 3: Group terms with $a$**\n$$"
      }, {
        "text": " mg - k_t Mg \u003d ma + Ma + \\frac{J^*}{R^2} a $$\n"
      }, {
        "text": "$$ g(m - k_t M) \u003d a \\left( m + M + \\frac{J^*}{R^2} \\"
      }, {
        "text": "right) $$\n\n**Step 4: Final Formula for Acceleration**\n$$ a \u003d g \\cdot \\frac{m - k_t"
      }, {
        "text": " M}{m + M + \\frac{J^*}{R^2}} $$\n\n\u003e [!tldr] **Interpretation"
      }, {
        "text": " of the Result**\n\u003e The numerator represents the **net driving force** (Gravity on hanging mass minus Friction on sliding"
      }, {
        "text": " mass).\n\u003e The denominator represents the **total inertia** of the system (Mass 1 + Mass 2 + Effective mass"
      }, {
        "text": " of the pulley $\\frac{J^*}{R^2}$).\n\n**Calculation (from notes):**\n$$ a \u003d 9"
      }, {
        "text": ".81 \\cdot \\frac{1 - 0.1(3)}{1 + 3 + \\frac"
      }, {
        "text": "{0.01}{0.1^2}} \u003d 9.81 \\cdot \\frac{0.7}{4"
      }, {
        "text": " + 1} \u003d 9.81 \\cdot \\frac{0.7}{5} \\approx 1.37"
      }, {
        "text": " \\, \\text{m/s}^2 $$\n*(Note: The student\u0027s note calculation resulted in 5.8."
      }, {
        "text": " Let\u0027s check the student\u0027s specific values. In the image, the result is $a\u003d5.8$,"
      }, {
        "text": " but checking the math: $\\frac{J^*}{R^2} \u003d \\frac{10^{-2}}{1"
      }, {
        "text": "0^{-2}} \u003d 1$. Denom is $1+3+1 \u003d 5$. Numerator $1 -"
      }, {
        "text": " 0.3 \u003d 0.7$. $0.7/5 \\cdot 10 \u003d 1.4"
      }, {
        "text": "$. The student likely used different mass values later or made a calculation error. **Warning: Check inputs.**)*\n\n---\n\n## 4."
      }, {
        "text": " Rolling Motion and Moment of Inertia\n\nCalculation of Moment of Inertia for a specific cylinder/wheel setup.\n\n*   **Given"
      }, {
        "text": ":** $a_t \u003d 0.16 \\, \\text{m/s}^2$ (Tangential acceleration?),"
      }, {

      }, {
        "text": "*   **Result:** $J^* \u003d \\frac{F_t R^2}{a_t}$\n*   **"

      }, {

        "text": "Hanging):} \u0026 \\quad m g - F_{v2} \u003d m a\n\\end{align}\n$$\n\n"
